blocks.text: I can identify and analyse layout and linguistic features of a diary entry.
Before we write a diary entry as the girl in ‘The Journey’, we need to know what a good diary entry contains.

items.title: Purpose and layout of a diary entry
Linguistic features of a diary entry

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: The aim of the text, the reason it was written.
A piece of writing that recalls an event or experience.
The way a text is structured.
A structure of language that uses words.

blocks.text: A diary is a personal book that a person writes in. Each time they write in it, that is called a **diary entry**.
The {purpose} of a diary entry is to **recount** important experiences and **express feelings**.
A diary is just for the writer to read. It is personal and private to them.

blocks.q: Sam writes in her diary about her first day at a new school and how nervous she felt. What is she doing?
options: Recounting an important experience and expressing her feelings
Telling other people about her life
blocks.why: A diary entry recounts important personal experiences and expresses feelings. It is private, so it is not for telling other people about your life or for a made-up story.

blocks.text: You will write a diary entry from the perspective of the girl in ‘The Journey’. It will recount what happened on the journey and express how she feels now, on a train close to safety.
In the model entry, the girl is called Leia. The book does not name her, so you can use Leia or choose your own name.

items: I am writing this from a train …

slides.title: The layout of a diary entry

blocks.text: **Layout** means the way the writing is organised on the page. A diary entry has four layout features.

items.title: Date
items.sub: written at the top on the left. It records when the entry was written

items.title: Greeting
items.sub: always ‘Dear Diary’ with a comma after

items.title: Paragraphs
items.sub: organise the recount in chronological order

items.title: Sign-off
items.sub: ends the entry. It is personal and can vary

blocks.q: Match each layout feature to its job.

pairs.b: records when the entry was written
organise the recount in chronological order
ends the entry, and is personal to the writer

blocks.q: Choose the correct answer about a diary entry.

items.q: What is at the very top, on the left?
What comes straight after the date?

blocks.text: Diary entries have special {linguistic features} to achieve their purpose. There are four to look for.

items.title: First person and informal language
items.sub: a personal piece of writing about yourself

items.title: Fronted adverbials of time
items.sub: to sequence events in time order

blocks.text: A diary entry is written in the **first person**, using the pronoun {I}. The language is **informal** because the writing is personal and private.
Here are ways informal language appears in the model entry:

items: Contractions: ‘I can’t believe how far we have travelled!’
CAPITAL LETTERS for emphasis: ‘we have FINALLY sat down!’
Exaggeration: ‘Home must be hundreds or maybe even thousands of miles away.’
Casual words: ‘how crazy the journey was going to be’

blocks.q: Is the sentence in diary style, or not?

items.text: I am SO happy to be on a seat!
She was pleased to be seated.
I can’t believe how far we have travelled!
The family had travelled a great distance.
My legs were wobbling like jelly.

blocks.text: A recount is about something that has already happened, so we use **past tense**. Diary entries use simple past and progressive past.

items.title: Simple past
items.sub: Every day, I wanted to rest

blocks.text: A fronted adverbial of time goes at the **front** of a sentence and tells us **when** something happened. It helps to put the events in chronological order.

blocks.label: See it in the model entry
blocks.text: **Then,** we spent a few nights on a ferry. **Yesterday,** I drew a picture in the dirt with a stick. Notice the comma after each one.

items.q: Which of these is a fronted adverbial of time?
Which of these is a fronted adverbial of time?
Why are fronted adverbials of time useful in a diary?
options: They help sequence the events in time order
They show that the writing is formal
They tell us the writer’s name

blocks.text: Towards the end of a diary entry, the writer often shifts from past to **present tense** to show how they feel **now**.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: A diary entry is not all in past tense. It uses past tense to recount events and present tense to express how the writer is feeling now.

blocks.q: Which sentence shows how the writer feels right now?
options: We ran away from a security guard.
blocks.why: ‘I miss my friends’ is in the present tense and shows a current feeling. The other two sentences recount past events.

slides.title: Analysing the features of diary entries

items: The purpose of a diary entry is to recount important personal experiences and to express feelings.
Layout: date, greeting (‘Dear Diary,’), paragraphs and a sign-off.
A diary entry is written in the first person and uses informal language.
Simple past and progressive past tenses recount what the writer experienced and felt.
Fronted adverbials of time sequence events in chronological order.
Present tense is used at points to show how the writer is feeling now.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a diary entry?
flashcards.back: To recount important personal experiences and to express feelings.

flashcards.front: Who is a diary written for?
flashcards.back: Only the writer. It is personal and private.
The way a text is structured.
A piece of writing that recalls an event or experience.

flashcards.front: Put the layout features of a diary entry in order.
flashcards.back: Date, greeting (‘Dear Diary,’), paragraphs to organise the recount, sign-off.

flashcards.front: What is the greeting in a diary entry?
What do paragraphs do in a diary entry?
flashcards.back: They organise the recount in chronological order.

flashcards.front: Which person is a diary entry written in?
Why is the language in a diary entry informal?
flashcards.back:
Because the writing is personal and private.

Example: I can’t believe how far we have travelled!

flashcards.front: Which tense recounts what the writer experienced?
flashcards.back:
Past tense (simple past and progressive past).

Example: I wanted to rest. My heart was pounding.

flashcards.front: What do fronted adverbials of time do?
flashcards.back:
They sequence events in a recount in chronological order.

Examples: Every day, Yesterday, Then,

flashcards.front: When does a diary entry shift into present tense?
flashcards.back:
When the writer expresses how they are feeling now.

Example: I miss my friends.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Analysing the features of diary entries
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: What is written at the very top of a diary entry, on the left side?
questions.explanation: The date is written at the top on the left and records when the entry was written.

questions.prompt: What is the greeting at the start of a diary entry? (Write the two words.)
questions.explanation: The greeting is always ‘Dear Diary’ followed by a comma.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark comes straight after ‘Dear Diary’?
questions.explanation: The greeting ‘Dear Diary,’ has a comma after it.

questions.prompt: Which part of a diary entry comes last?
questions.explanation: A sign-off ends the diary entry.

questions.prompt: What is the word for a piece of writing that recalls an event or experience?
questions.explanation: A recount is a piece of writing that recalls an event or experience.

questions.prompt: A diary entry uses the pronoun ‘I’. Which person is it written in: first, second or third?
questions.explanation: A diary entry is written in the first person using the pronoun ‘I’.

questions.prompt: Which tense does the writer use to recount what happened in a diary entry?
questions.explanation: A recount is about something that has already happened, so it uses past tense.

questions.prompt: Which kind of phrase, such as ‘Yesterday,’ or ‘Then,’ at the start of a sentence, helps put events in time order?
questions.explanation: Fronted adverbials of time sequence events chronologically.

questions.prompt: Which tense shows how the writer is feeling now, such as ‘I miss my friends’?
questions.explanation: A diary entry shifts into present tense to express how the writer is currently feeling.
